explanations: terra: People are commanded to worship their Rabb, who created them and those before them. It grounds worship in the Creator-nurturer rather than in an unknown master.

luna: The section’s recap names the Lord who feeds clouds and plants; this ayah pairs the sky as canopy with rain sent down and fruits brought forth as provision. | terra: The same Rabb makes earth a resting place, sky a canopy, and rain a source of fruit provision. Ground, water, plant, and dependence form one worship scene.
terra: When guidance comes, those who follow it have no fear and do not grieve. It makes following the given road the opposite of exposed strayness.

luna: The section’s weary servant asks his Lord for help; this ayah commands people to seek help (اسْتَعِينُوا) through patience and prayer, a direct use of the same help-root as the section’s “nastaʿīn.” | terra: “Seek help through patience and prayer” is hard except for the humble. It supplies a Qur’anic form for the section’s worshipper who asks the owner for help.
luna: This continues the call to seek help in 2:45: the humble are certain they will meet their Lord and return to Him, matching the section’s servant addressing the owner at the end of a journey.

luna: The section’s dictionary form “muzallal” (مذلل) is a tamed camel; this cow is specifically said not to plow earth or water a field, a boundary case for an animal’s being made useful or subdued. | terra: The cow is described as not ذَلُولٌ, not broken to plough earth or water crops. This negative boundary sharpens the section’s “müzellel” animal/path sense and its link to earth and water.

luna: The section’s road has an arrival House; this ayah identifies the House as a place of return and safety and commands Abraham and Ishmael to purify it for worshippers. | terra: The House is made a place of return and safety, with Abraham’s standing-place made a prayer place. It realizes the section’s return-home and upright-worship imagery.
luna: Abraham and Ishmael raise the House’s foundations and ask God to accept their work, joining the section’s Ibrahim, House, and worship images.
terra: “God’s dye/mark” (صِبْغَةَ ٱللَّهِ) is followed by “we are worshippers of Him.” It gives the section’s brand image a mark that identifies voluntary worship rather than an idol.
terra: God’s direction of faces is “so that I may complete My favor upon you and so that you may be guided.” Completion and way-finding are explicitly paired.
terra: Believers are told to seek help through patience and prayer, with God with the patient. It turns the requested aid of 1:5 into a sustained way of walking.
luna: This ayah gathers heaven and earth, winds, clouds, and rain that revives the earth into signs, closely matching the section’s linked cloud-and-growth image.
terra: Completing the counted days is followed by magnifying God for having guided you. It echoes the section’s 22:37 meeting of completion, praise, and guidance.

luna: The section’s herd is separated for sacrifice and brought to its destination; this ayah says the offering must reach its place (مَحِلَّهُ), within the completion of pilgrimage for God. | terra: Completing pilgrimage includes an available sacrifice, and the offering must reach its place before a head is shaved. It joins completion, animal, and destination at the House.

luna: This ayah names nursing a child for two full years and the parents’ duty to provide, a specific continuation of the section’s child-rearing image. | terra: Mothers nurse for two complete years “for whoever wishes to complete nursing.” The verse supplies the section’s precise boundary at which nurture reaches completion.

luna: The section contrasts a sign with its Lord; Abraham answers a king’s claim by challenging him to bring the sun from the west after God brings it from the east, exposing the created sun’s limits. | terra: In disputing over his Lord, Abraham answers a false sovereign with God’s bringing the sun from the east; the ruler is confounded and not guided. Sovereignty, rising sun, and guidance converge.
terra: A creditor must defer a debtor in hardship, and remission is better. It supplies the merciful human relation that the debt-accounting passage leaves at stake.
terra: The immediately preceding warning says every soul will return to God and be paid in full for what it earned. It gives the contract’s careful accounting its final Day horizon.

luna: The section names this debt passage’s term, witness’s “tadill” (تضلّ, lapse/forget), and “aqwam” (أقوم, more upright); the ayah contrasts a witness’s possible lapse with writing that is more upright and evidentially sound. | terra: The debt verse fixes term, writing, witnesses, the possibility that one may “go astray/forget” (تَضِلَّ), and testimony that is more upright (أَقْوَمُ). It concretizes debt, lostness, and standing straight.

luna: The section includes the womb as a place of divine forming; this ayah says God shapes people in wombs as He wills. | terra: God forms people in wombs as He wills. It gives the section’s formative mercy an explicit divine act rather than an impersonal growth.

luna: The section moves from the known owner to the day property is gathered under one ruler; this ayah says dominion belongs to God and that He gives and takes it as He wills. | terra: God is addressed as owner of sovereignty, giving and taking rule, honoring and humbling. It unfolds the section’s Malik image as active possession and reversal.
terra: Jesus calls God “my Lord and your Lord,” then says “worship Him; this is a straight path”; the true Rabb, direct address, worship, and road remain one claim.
terra: The first House set for people at Bakkah is blessed and “guidance for the worlds.” It gives the section’s road an endpoint that is both a house and guidance.
terra: The House contains clear signs and pilgrimage is due from whoever can find a way to it. The verse makes finding the road to the House a duty before the true owner.
terra: Whoever holds fast to God has been guided to a straight path. The verse makes dependence on the true owner the grip that prevents straying.

luna: The section says the judgment-day faces carry a divided outcome; this ayah depicts faces darkened and asks whether they disbelieved after faith, attaching the dark face to punishment. | terra: On the Day some faces are whitened and some blackened; the blackened faces are confronted with punishment. It gives the section’s two judgment-faces a sharp visual division.

luna: This is the other face of 3:106: faces are bright and enter God’s mercy, matching the section’s paired faces of wrath and favor. | terra: Those whose faces are whitened remain in God’s mercy. It supplies the favorable face’s lasting relation to divine mercy.

luna: The section joins approval and wrath to the account day; this ayah directly contrasts following God’s pleasure (رِضْوَانَ اللَّهِ) with incurring His anger (سَخَطٍ), whose destination is Hell. | terra: Following God’s pleasure is set against returning with His anger and Hell. It gives the section’s rıza/gazap division a direct final-destination contrast.
terra: God says obedience would guide them to a straight path. It makes the section’s prayed-for route an enacted response rather than a mere direction.

luna: The section’s wording “those You favored” (أنعمت عليهم) is made concrete here: those who obey God and the Messenger join the prophets, truthful, martyrs, and righteous whom God favored. | terra: Those who obey God and the Messenger are with those God has favored. It identifies the “those You favored” of the section’s path by their companionship and obedience.
terra: Believers are commanded to stand firmly for justice even against themselves or relatives. It gives the section’s standing balance an embodied witness.
terra: Those who hold fast to God receive mercy and bounty and are guided to Him by a straight path. It gives the road a destination in God Himself.
terra: The command names sacrificial animals, their garlands, and those heading for the Sacred House seeking bounty and pleasure. It joins the guide/offering word-field to a directed journey home.

luna: The section’s phrase “completion of favor” meets this ayah’s explicit “I have perfected My favor upon you” (أَتْمَمْتُ عَلَيْكُمْ نِعْمَتِي), identifying completion as a divine gift. | terra: God announces that He has perfected religion, completed His favor, and approved submission. The section’s completed blessing reaches its communal and worshipful form here.
terra: After purification for prayer, God says He intends to complete His favor so people may give thanks. It links finished favor to the worshipper’s bodily approach.
terra: Believers are commanded to stand firmly for God as witnesses with justice, without hatred bending them. It turns uprightness into a refusal to tilt judgment.
terra: God guides those who seek His pleasure to ways of peace and brings them from darkness to light. Divine pleasure becomes a route, answering the section’s angry fall from the way.

luna: This ayah says those under God’s curse and anger are made apes and swine, a specific outcome for the section’s category of those under wrath. | terra: Those cursed and angered by God are described as farther astray from the sound way. It directly binds غضب, straying, and the section’s two endings of the road.
terra: People who went astray, led many astray, and wandered from the even way are named as a warning. It gives the section’s lost herd a human, imitated path of deviation.
terra: An expiation can be livestock “as an offering reaching the Kaʿbah” (هَدْيًا بَٰلِغَ ٱلْكَعْبَةِ); it gives the section’s home-bound sacrifice its exact arrival.

luna: The section links a herd offering to the House; this ayah names the Kaaba, the Sacred House, as a place of standing for people and names sacrificial offerings among its sacred markers. | terra: The Kaʿbah, sacred month, sacrificial animals, and garlands are made a قيامًا for people. The House, herd, and the section’s image of standing are gathered in one verse.
terra: Land creatures and birds are communities like people, and all are gathered to their Lord. It gives the herd its own communal relation to the known Rabb and final gathering.
luna: Before Abraham’s night scene, he challenges his father for taking idols as gods; this supplies the rejection of false lords behind the section’s distinction between sign and Lord.

luna: This immediately introduces Abraham’s night scene by saying God showed him the dominion of the heavens and earth so he could be certain, supplying the created order behind the signs. | terra: God shows Abraham the dominion of heavens and earth before the star, moon, and sun scene. It frames those objects as signs within divine dominion.

luna: This begins the section’s night sequence: Abraham watches a star set and rejects it as Lord when it disappears, treating the celestial body as a sign rather than the Creator. | terra: Abraham sees a rising star, calls it “my Lord,” then rejects it when it sets. It begins the section’s test of a rising sign against the true Rabb.

luna: In the section’s night scene Abraham watches the moon set and says that without his Lord’s guidance he would be among the lost; the ayah uses “al-ḍāllīn” (الضالين), the same root/form family as the section’s “lost” ending. | terra: With the moon, Abraham says that unless his Lord guides him he will be among the ضَالِّينَ. Celestial appearance, true guidance, and lostness meet explicitly.

luna: After the star and moon in 6:76–77, Abraham watches the sun set and says he is clear of the people’s association, completing the section’s sequence of fading celestial signs. | terra: The rising sun is called larger, then rejected at its setting; Abraham disavows association. It completes the section’s sequence of elevated but non-divine signs.

luna: After the star, moon, and sun set in the section’s cited night scene, Abraham turns his face to the Creator of the heavens and earth, distinguishing the rising signs from the Lord they indicate. | terra: Abraham turns his face to the Originator of heavens and earth as a hanīf, not an associator. It names the true referent behind the signs.
luna: The section asks for the straight path of those favored; this ayah names prophets and righteous people whom God chose and guided to a straight path.
luna: After naming prophets guided to a straight path in 6:87, this ayah says that is God’s guidance, supporting the section’s requested guidance for the favored community.
luna: The section’s “hādī” guide for the traveler meets this ayah’s stars, made as guidance through the darknesses of land and sea.
luna: The section says the herd is named for God before sacrifice; this ayah commands eating from livestock over which God’s name has been mentioned.
luna: This is the boundary of 6:118’s named offering: the ayah forbids eating from what has not had God’s name mentioned, linking the section’s naming detail to a clear limit.
terra: “This is the path of your Lord, straight”; the signs are detailed for those who remember. It links path, Rabb, and recognisable signs as the section does.
luna: This ayah asks whether messengers came from among jinn and humans to warn of meeting this day, joining the section’s account day to being warned and addressed.

luna: The section distinguishes the straight path from deviation; this ayah commands following God’s one straight path and forbids following other paths that divide people from it. | terra: “This is My straight path, so follow it; do not follow the ways” makes a single owned route stand against paths that scatter people from it.
luna: This ayah says the Book was given to Moses to complete God’s favor upon the good-doer and as guidance and mercy, bringing the section’s Moses, completed gift, and path together.
terra: The Prophet says his Lord has guided him to a straight path, an upright religion, the creed of Abraham. It connects the requested road to Abraham’s anti-idolatrous orientation.

luna: The section says the owned person turns willingly to the owner; this ayah has the speaker say his prayer, sacrifice, life, and death belong to God, Lord of the worlds. | terra: “My prayer and my sacrifice, my living and my dying are for God, Lord of the worlds.” Sacrifice is here explicitly owned by the Rabb rather than by a merely human keeper.

luna: The section joins measure to reckoning; this ayah says weighing on that day is truth, making the scale a standard for judgment. | terra: The weighing on that Day is truth, and heavy scales bring success. It gives the section’s level balance its decisive outcome.

luna: This gives the opposite result in 7:8: those whose scales are light have lost themselves, joining the section’s measure to a way lost. | terra: Those whose scales are light lose themselves because they wronged the signs. It supplies the opposite fate of the upright measure.
terra: Satan vows to sit in wait on God’s straight path. It gives the section’s journey an active obstructer rather than only an abstract crooked way.
terra: Satan says he will approach people from before, behind, right, and left to make them ungrateful. It fills out how the obstruction around the straight path operates.
terra: One party is guided while another merits error because it took devils as protectors instead of God. False patronage becomes the mechanism of thinking oneself guided while lost.

luna: The section joins cloud, rain, and the Lord nurturing plants; this ayah describes winds carrying heavy clouds, rain sent to a dead land, and fruit brought forth from it. | terra: Winds carry heavy clouds, rain is sent to dead land, and fruits emerge. The section’s cloud-and-plant nurture is staged as renewal from God.
terra: Good land yields vegetation by its Lord’s permission while bad land yields only scant growth. It gives nourishment a moral and relational contrast without changing the scene.
terra: Shuʿayb commands worship of the one God, full measure and weight, and no defrauding. Worship and an unbent balance are one public way.
terra: Moses tells his people to seek help from God and be patient, because the earth belongs to God. It joins help, endurance, and the true owner of the ground on which they walk.
terra: Moses’ thirty-night appointment is completed with ten, so his Lord’s term becomes forty nights. It gives the section’s completion-at-a-boundary image a Moses-and-Rabb form.
luna: The section pairs wrath with a lost way; this ayah says wrath and humiliation will overtake those who took the calf, a specific scene of divine anger after idolatry.
terra: People who do not use heart, eyes, or ears are “like livestock—rather, more astray.” The herd image becomes a warning against human loss of the way.
terra: Gardens and lasting dwellings are followed by the declaration that God’s pleasure is greater. It distinguishes the giver’s pleasure from the gifts of the final home.

luna: The section says the road has an arrival house; this ayah says God calls to the Home of Peace and guides whom He wills to a straight path. | terra: God calls to the Home of Peace and guides whom He wills to a straight path. It names both the destination-house and the road toward it.
terra: Those who do good receive the best and more, and neither dust nor humiliation covers their faces. It directly answers the section’s dust-covered Day-face.
terra: Hūd says his Lord is upon a straight path. The true Rabb is not merely beside the road but the reliable order by which it is straight.
terra: Shuʿayb calls his people to worship God alone and not diminish measure or weight. The verse joins the true master to the exact fraud scene.
terra: He commands full measure and just weight and warns of an encompassing Day’s punishment. It binds market balance directly to the Day of account.
terra: Jacob says the Lord will complete His favor on Joseph and Jacob’s family as before. It supplies the section’s completed نعمة as an act of the knowing Rabb.
luna: The section’s dictionary forms “neʿāmah” (beam) and “qāmah” (pulley) meet at the well; this ayah explicitly sends a water-drawer down with his bucket into a well.
terra: Joseph asks whether many separate lords are better or God, the One, the Overpowering. It turns the ownerless animal image into a question of whom one truly belongs to.

luna: The section distinguishes a sign or name from what it points to; Joseph says the gods worshipped besides Allah are only names people have named, with no authority, then says judgment belongs to God alone and commands worship of Him. | terra: Joseph says judgment belongs only to God, who commanded worship of Him; that is the upright religion. Ownership, worship, and a right way cohere in his prison speech.
terra: God knows what every womb bears and each decrease or increase within it; everything has a measure with Him. It precisely joins womb, hidden growth, and measure.
luna: This ayah describes revelation as bringing people from darkness into light by their Lord’s permission and to the path of the Mighty, Praiseworthy, a specific guidance-to-path formulation.

luna: The section invokes “the days of God” (أَيَّامِ اللَّهِ) as days of divergent outcomes; here Moses is commanded to remind his people of those days, with signs for the patient and grateful. | terra: Moses is told to remind his people of “the days of God,” signs for the patient and grateful. It gives the section’s days a history of punishment and favor, not a neutral calendar.
luna: The section’s Lord completes gifts; this ayah says God has given people from all they asked, yet they could not count His favor, making abundance and its uncountability explicit.
terra: Abraham settles descendants near the Sacred House, asks that hearts incline toward it, and asks for fruit provision. House, directed longing, and sustenance meet in his prayer.
terra: Abraham asks forgiveness for believers on the Day when the account will stand. It joins Abraham, standing, and the section’s Day of debt-accounting.
terra: God says, “This is a straight path to Me.” It makes the straight road’s endpoint the Lord Himself.
terra: Satan has no authority over God’s servants except those who follow him among the astray. It marks the boundary between owned servants and the lost followers.

luna: This begins the section’s herd passage: livestock supply warmth, benefits, and food, giving concrete content to the Lord’s provision. | terra: God creates livestock for warmth, benefits, and food; this grounds the section’s herd in provision from the Rabb rather than in an ownerless animal.

luna: The section places the herd’s pasture journey next to the guidance of 16:9; this ayah specifically names the beauty of livestock when driven out in the morning and brought back in the evening. | terra: The livestock’s beauty appears when they return at evening and go out to pasture; it is the herd’s outward journey and return immediately before the path of 16:9.

luna: The section’s traveler and herd meet in the livestock passage: this ayah says the animals carry people and their loads to a town they could not reach without hardship. | terra: The animals carry people’s burdens to a land they could reach only with hardship; it gives the section’s weary traveller and animal-road image its concrete travel burden.

luna: The section joins the herd to the road and a traveler’s mount; this ayah names horses, mules, and donkeys as mounts and adornment. | terra: Horses, mules, and donkeys are made for riding and adornment; this extends the passage’s movement along a road through animals fitted to carry people.

luna: The section sets herd and road together: the passage just described cattle going out to pasture and returning (16:6), and this ayah says the straight route is God’s while some routes deviate (جائر). | terra: “Upon God is the direction of the way,” while some ways are crooked (جَائِرٌ); this is the section’s herdsman-guide scene stated as a divine distinction between a straight route and deviation.

luna: The section’s recap names cloud and vegetation among the Lord’s gifts; this ayah says God sends down rainwater for people to drink and for plants to grow. | terra: Rain becomes drink and vegetation in which livestock pasture; it joins the section’s water, plant, herd, and sustaining-Rabb images in the same sequence as the road passage.

luna: Continuing the rain in 16:10, this ayah names crops, olives, palms, grapes, and other fruits as growing from it, making provision visible in the land. | terra: By rain God grows crops, olives, dates, grapes, and all fruits. It extends the nearby pasture-water scene into the plant nourishment named in the section.
luna: This ayah says God set mountains, rivers, and paths on earth so people may be guided, joining the landscape and wayfinding images in the section.
luna: Continuing the landmarks and paths in 16:15, this ayah says people are guided by landmarks and stars, meeting the section’s guide for travelers and herd.
luna: This repeats the section’s idea of completed favor as a gift beyond counting: if people tried to count God’s favors, they could not enumerate them.
luna: This ayah says God sends water from the sky and revives the earth after its death, a specific water-and-life parallel to the section’s cloud-fed vegetation.
terra: God contrasts a powerless owned slave with one freely given good provision who spends it. It makes the section’s owner, dependency, and bestowed provision concrete.

terra: One dependent servant is a burden to his master wherever directed, while the other commands justice and is on a straight path. It makes servitude, direction, burden, and upright road a single parable.

luna: This ayah says people are brought from their mothers’ wombs knowing nothing and given hearing, sight, and hearts, a direct account of the womb and the Lord’s provision after birth. | terra: God brings people from their mothers’ wombs knowing nothing, then gives hearing, sight, and hearts for gratitude. It gives nurture a path from hidden formation to response.
terra: After naming shelters, shade, and protective provision, God says He completes His favor so people may submit. It joins nurture, shelter, completion, and willing servitude.
terra: Abraham is chosen and guided to a straight path after being grateful for God’s favors. It joins gratitude for نعمة to the Abrahamic road.
terra: The Qur’an guides to what is most upright. Its أَقْوَم language links the debt verse’s upright testimony to the section’s upright road.

luna: The section links “Rabb” with raising a child; this prayer asks God for mercy “as they raised me when small” (رَبَّيَانِي صَغِيرًا), directly joining nurture and Lordship. | terra: The prayer asks mercy for parents “as they raised me small” (رَبَّيَانِى). It gives non-coercive human nurture the merciful counterpart to Pharaoh’s boast.

luna: The section names the balance and fraud in measurement; this command pairs full measure with a straight balance (مستقيم), making upright measure a concrete duty. | terra: The command to give full measure and weigh with the upright balance uses the language of straightness. It makes the section’s scale and straight road share an ethical posture.
luna: This ayah describes people gathered on their faces on the Day of Resurrection, a specific adverse reversal of the section’s upright traveler.
terra: God may be called Allah or the Merciful, for His are the most beautiful names. It lets the section’s opening name hold both divine identity and the Rahman/Rahim relation.
luna: This ayah shows rain making vegetation grow and then becoming dry debris scattered by the wind, a specific parallel to provision that passes away.
luna: The section portrays a weary traveler needing guidance and help; Moses and his companion here say their journey has brought them fatigue, a concrete road-weariness parallel.

luna: The section links a lapse of memory with disappearance from the way; during Moses’s journey, his companion says he forgot the fish and it took its way into the sea, a concrete but indirect meeting of forgetting and loss.
luna: After the lost fish in 18:63, Moses recognizes it as what they sought and they retrace their tracks; this ayah contributes the return along a path, not the forgetting that began the episode.
terra: Jesus again joins the shared Lordship of God to “worship Him” and “a straight path,” confirming that the section’s road is a relation to its real owner.

luna: The section’s wording “those You favored” (أنعمت عليهم) has a concrete parallel in the prophets God favored; this ayah shows them falling in prostration when the Merciful’s signs are recited. | terra: These are the prophets “whom God favored”; when the Merciful’s verses are recited, they fall prostrate and weep. Favor is shown as receptive, willing worship.
luna: God tells Moses He has already bestowed another favor on him, introducing the infancy account that follows and the section’s theme of gifts beyond Pharaoh’s claimed nurture.
luna: This continues the favor in 20:37 by recalling the revelation to Moses’s mother, part of the care that preserved the infant before Pharaoh’s household took him.

luna: Continuing the infancy account, Moses is placed in a chest and the river carries him to the bank; this supplies the concrete preservation behind God’s favor in 20:37. | terra: God directs the infant Moses through the river and says He cast love upon him so that he would be brought up under God’s care. It is true nurture beneath Pharaoh’s household.

luna: The section contrasts Pharaoh’s claim to have raised Moses with the true Lord’s care; this ayah recounts Moses being returned to his mother so she could be comforted and not grieve. | terra: Moses is returned to his mother so her eye may be comforted, then saved and tested. It completes the divine care that contrasts with Pharaoh’s later boast of raising him.
luna: After Pharaoh asks who their Lord is, this ayah gives the question that leads to Moses’s answer about God giving each thing its form and guidance in 20:50.

luna: Moses says his Lord gave everything its form and then guided it; the section joins the Lord who forms and nurtures with the guide who leads on a path. | terra: Moses defines the real Lord to Pharaoh as the one who gives every thing its creation and then guides it. It fuses true Rabbhood, fitting a creature, and leading it onward.
luna: Moses says his Lord neither errs nor forgets (لَا يَضِلُّ رَبِّي وَلَا يَنْسَى); this gives a specific contrast to the section’s witness who may “tadill” (تضلّ, lapse) in 2:282.

luna: The section’s road and cloud-to-plant images meet in this ayah: God makes earth a cradle, lays out paths, sends water from heaven, and brings out varied vegetation. | terra: God makes earth a cradle, makes paths through it, and sends water from the sky to bring out pairs of plants. It directly unites road, water, and sustaining formation.
terra: “Eat and pasture your livestock” follows the road-and-water verse. It gives the section’s herd its share in the same divine provision.
luna: This ayah says people were created from earth, returned to it, and brought forth again, linking the section’s earth, death, and account-day images.
terra: Moses is commanded to make a dry path through the sea for the Children of Israel. It gives water-and-road a direct Exodus form.
luna: This ayah recalls God’s deliverance of Israel from Pharaoh and His meeting promise to Moses, a neighboring account of rescue from the false ruler described in the section.

luna: The section explicitly joins divine anger to falling: this ayah says whoever incurs God’s anger has “fallen” (هَوَىٰ), a concrete reversal of its upright path and standing images. | terra: God warns that whoever His anger settles upon “has fallen” (فَقَدْ هَوَىٰ). The section’s anger descending and the traveller’s fall are the verse’s own physical verdict.

luna: Immediately after the fall under wrath in 20:81, this ayah describes the one who repents, believes, and acts rightly as then guided; it supplies the recovery side of the section’s fall/way contrast. | terra: After repentance, faith, and good work, God says He forgives and then guides. It supplies the risen, reoriented counterpart to the fall under anger in 20:81.
terra: Moses says he hastened to his Lord so that He might be pleased. This is the immediate positive counterpart to the anger-and-guidance sequence of 20:81–82.

luna: The section contrasts falling under wrath with finding the way; this ayah says whoever follows God’s guidance will neither go astray (يَضِلُّ) nor be wretched, making guidance the stated boundary against loss. | terra: After descent, God promises guidance; whoever follows it will neither go astray nor suffer. It supplies a direct answer to the section’s fear of becoming lost.

luna: The section brings the scale and people standing on the account day together; this ayah says just scales will be set for the Resurrection and no soul will be wronged. | terra: Just balances are set up for the Day of Resurrection, with even a mustard seed brought forth. The verse makes the section’s scale explicitly a final accounting device.

luna: This ayah describes womb development through stages until a stated term and maturity, a concrete parallel to the section’s growth toward completion. | terra: What God wills remains in wombs to an appointed term, then emerges a child and reaches full strength. It maps the section’s growth toward its measured completion.
terra: Sun, moon, stars, mountains, trees, animals, and many people prostrate to God. Celestial signs, herd, and worship are gathered under the Creator rather than worshipping one another.

terra: God assigns Abraham the site of the House, commands no association, and tells him to purify it for circling, standing, bowing, and prostration. It supplies the worshipful home at the road’s end.

luna: The section’s road ends at the House; this ayah calls people to pilgrimage to the House from every distant pass, making the route and destination explicit. | terra: Pilgrims come walking and on lean camels from every distant pass. It gives the section’s road a bodily journey whose destination is the House.

luna: This continues the pilgrimage call: it says to mention God’s name over livestock He provided on appointed days, then eat and feed the needy. | terra: At the pilgrimage people mention God’s name over the livestock He provided, then eat and feed the needy; herd, divine name, provision, and purposeful arrival coincide.

luna: This continues the pilgrimage route in 22:27: the ayah’s rites culminate in fulfilling vows and circumambulating the ancient House, the destination in the section’s image. | terra: Pilgrims complete their rites and circumambulate the Ancient House. Its own contribution is the final arrival and circling that follows the sacrifice passage.
terra: Honoring God’s symbols is said to arise from piety of hearts. It explains why the animals in the neighboring rites are signs rather than ends in themselves.

luna: This continues the sacrificial-animal passage: livestock have benefits until an appointed term, and their destination is the ancient House. | terra: The sacrificial animals have benefits until an appointed term, then their place is at the Ancient House; it is the section’s animal carried onward to its home.

luna: The section links livestock, naming, and the House; this ayah appoints a rite for every community so they mention God’s name over livestock He provided, then commands submission to Him. | terra: Each community is given a rite to mention God’s name over provided livestock, followed by “submit to Him.” This makes sacrifice a voluntary servitude to the one God.

luna: The section brings herd, sacrifice, naming, and submission together; this ayah describes sacrificial camels as among God’s rites, says God’s name is mentioned over them, and calls them made subject to people. | terra: The camels are God’s symbols: His name is spoken over them, they fall, and people eat and feed others. It supplies the fully staged sacrificial-herd scene behind the section’s meeting.

luna: The section’s “hādī” guide and sacrificial herd meet in this ayah: it names the offering (هدي) and says God has guided people (هداكم), while explaining that piety, not flesh or blood, reaches Him. | terra: God subdues the animals so people may magnify Him “for what He guided you to” (عَلَىٰ مَا هَدَىٰكُمْ). It explicitly joins tamed herd, praise, and guidance on the way.
terra: Those given knowledge recognize revelation as truth, believe, and their hearts humble; God guides believers to a straight path. This joins knowledge, submission, and route.
luna: The section joins the womb to the Lord who forms and raises; this ayah begins a specific sequence of human creation from clay and then a drop placed in a secure lodging.
luna: This continues 23:12’s creation sequence by locating the drop in the womb, the section’s explicit image of nurture and formation.

luna: This completes the womb sequence from 23:12–13 through staged formation to a new creation, matching the section’s growth toward completion. | terra: The embryo’s successive formations culminate in “another creation.” This makes the section’s shaped-in-the-womb image a sequence of deliberate making.
luna: The section says the Lord nurtures plants through clouds and rain; this ayah says water is sent down in due measure and kept on earth, making provision measured rather than ownerless.
luna: Continuing the measured water in 23:18, this ayah names gardens of palms and grapes and fruits as its yield, connecting rain to completed provision.
terra: Livestock contain a lesson: people drink from them, receive benefits, and eat. It gives the section’s herd its provision and instruction together.
terra: People are carried on livestock and ships. It extends the animal from provision into the traveller’s means of passage.
luna: The section places standing and a balance on the account day; this ayah says those whose scales are heavy will succeed, stating the favorable result of that image.
luna: This is the adverse outcome paired with 23:102: those whose scales are light have lost themselves, connecting the section’s balance to loss.
terra: Every living creature is created from water, with distinct ways of moving. It links water, formed creatures, and the animal movement beneath the section’s road imagery.
terra: God guides whom He wills to a straight path. Its own contribution is the guidance that follows the water-created creatures of 24:45.
luna: The section contrasts face-down stumbling with upright walking on the straight path; this ayah says those gathered on their faces to Hell are worse in destination and more astray.
terra: Those who neither hear nor reason are likened to livestock, “rather more astray in way.” It directly reverses the section’s guided herd and leader.

luna: This ayah describes God sending winds as glad tidings before mercy and sending down pure water, directly meeting the section’s cloud-and-provision image. | terra: God sends winds as mercy and sends down purifying water from the sky. It gives the section’s cloud-water provision a merciful source.

luna: Continuing the rain in 25:48, this ayah says the water revives a dead land and gives drink to livestock and people, completing the section’s cloud-to-herd provision. | terra: That water revives dead land and gives drink to livestock and many people. It explicitly distributes the provision to herd and traveller together.

luna: The section’s root/form “rabba” (رَبَّى, to rear) appears in Pharaoh’s claim that he raised Moses as a child; the scene sets a human claimant to nurturing beside Moses’s true Lord. | terra: Pharaoh says, “Did we not raise you among us as a child?” (نُرَبِّكَ). The source section’s raising word becomes a coercive claim of false nurture.

luna: This is Pharaoh’s accusation immediately before Moses’s answer in 26:20: he calls the deed an act and Moses ungrateful, giving the “lost” reply its debate context. | terra: Pharaoh follows his claimed upbringing by indicting Moses for his deed and calling him among the ungrateful. Its accusation exposes the pressure beneath the supposed favor of 26:18.

luna: Moses answers Pharaoh’s charge by saying he acted while among “the lost/unknowing” (الضالين); the section connects this word-family to its final image of being lost from the way. | terra: Moses says he acted while among the ضَالِّينَ. In the same exchange, lostness answers Pharaoh’s claimed raising and anticipates the section’s road imagery.

luna: Immediately after Moses’s “lost” wording in 26:20, he says his Lord gave him judgment and made him a messenger; this is the section’s contrast between Pharaoh’s claimed nurture and the true Lord’s gift. | terra: After fleeing in fear, Moses says “my Lord gave me judgment and made me one of the messengers.” The real Rabb gives vocation where Pharaoh claimed a debt.

luna: The section points to Pharaoh’s “favor” claim and the enslavement of Israel in one sentence; this ayah names that forced enslavement, reversing a supposed act of care into oppression. | terra: Moses calls Pharaoh’s alleged favor the fact that he enslaved the Children of Israel. It is the section’s decisive reversal: imposed bondage masquerading as nurture versus chosen worship.
luna: After the section’s exchange about raising Moses and his Lord’s gifts (26:18–22), Pharaoh asks what the Lord of the worlds is, putting the true Lord at the center of their dispute.

luna: This answers Pharaoh’s question in 26:23: Moses identifies the Lord as Lord of the heavens, earth, and what lies between, enlarging the section’s contrast between a ruler and the true Rabb. | terra: Moses answers Pharaoh that the true Lord is Lord of the heavens, earth, and what lies between them. It replaces Pharaoh’s claimed nurture with cosmic Rabbhood.
luna: This continues the exchange about the Lord of the worlds: Pharaoh addresses the surrounding chiefs after Moses identifies the Lord, showing his rejection of the answer.
luna: Continuing Moses’s answer in 26:24, this ayah names “your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers,” directly placing Pharaoh himself under the Lord whose nurture he claims.
luna: Pharaoh calls Moses mad after Moses names the Lord of the worlds; this is a concrete hostile response within the section’s contrast between false ruler and true Rabb.

luna: Moses answers that the Lord of the east and west and what lies between them is the true Lord, extending the section’s distinction between created signs and their Lord. | terra: Moses further names the Lord of east, west, and what lies between them. The verse turns the dispute over possession into orientation under the real Lord.
luna: Pharaoh threatens to imprison Moses after the Lord-of-worlds exchange, turning his claim to authority into coercion, as in the section’s contrast between service and enslavement.
terra: Moses strikes the sea and it splits into towering parts. It supplies the water that becomes passable space for the guided people.

luna: The section cites Abraham’s sequence: his Lord created him and “guides me” (يهدين); this ayah gives the guidance link in Abraham’s own account of his Lord. | terra: Abraham calls God the one who created him and then guides him. It begins the section’s ordered confession with formation becoming a personal route.

luna: Continuing 26:78, Abraham says his Lord feeds and gives him drink, the provision that the section places between guidance and hope for forgiveness on the Day of Recompense. | terra: Abraham says God feeds him and gives him drink. It supplies the water and nourishment step after guidance.

luna: This continues Abraham’s account of his Lord’s care in 26:78–79: he says that when he is ill, God heals him, a specific act of provision on the same path of dependence. | terra: Abraham adds that when he is ill, God heals him. Its bodily need continues the same speech of dependence between drinking and death.

luna: Abraham continues from healing to death and resurrection; this makes the Day of Recompense in 26:82 the end of the life sequence developed by the section. | terra: God causes Abraham to die and will bring him to life. This is the passage’s bridge from daily provision toward its Day-of-recompense ending.

luna: The section cites Abraham hoping that his Lord forgives him on “the Day of Recompense” (يوم الدين), bringing the section’s Lord, dependence, and reckoning together in the speaker’s own words. | terra: Abraham hopes that God will forgive him on the Day of Recompense. It supplies the section’s final dīn-day step in the same first-person sequence.
terra: “Give full measure” and do not be among those who cause loss. It names the receiving side of the scale that the section makes answerable to judgment.
terra: “Weigh with the straight balance” makes the section’s uprightness literal in commercial measurement.
terra: Do not deprive people of their due or spread corruption in the land. It gives the imbalance a social consequence beyond the instrument itself.

luna: The section’s sun-worshippers miss the distinction between sign and Lord; this ayah says the Queen of Sheba’s people prostrate to the sun and that Satan bars them from the way. | terra: A people prostrate to the sun instead of God; Satan beautifies this and bars them from the way, so they are not guided. It is the section’s exact failure to distinguish sign from its Lord.

luna: This continues 27:24’s sun-worship scene: the ayah asks why they do not prostrate to God, who brings forth what is hidden in the heavens and earth, completing the section’s sign-versus-signified distinction. | terra: The following call is to prostrate to God, who brings out what is hidden in heavens and earth. It states the corrective object of worship to 27:24’s sun worship.
luna: This completes the Sheba passage’s corrective to sun-worship: God alone is God and Lord of the mighty throne, naming the Lord whom the sign should point toward.

luna: The section describes an opening name as a raised identifying sign; this ayah says Solomon’s letter is “from Solomon” and begins with “In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful,” using the divine name to mark the message’s source.
luna: This ayah asks who guides people in the darknesses of land and sea and sends winds before mercy, joining the section’s wayfinding and cloud/rain scenes.

luna: The section’s child-rearing image has its other side here: Moses’s mother is told to nurse him, then place him in the river without fear, under God’s promise to return him and make him a messenger.
luna: This continues 28:7: Pharaoh’s household picks up the infant Moses, setting up the human foster-care claim that the section reads against God’s care.
luna: Pharaoh’s household takes the infant Moses in this ayah, and Pharaoh’s wife asks that he be kept as a child; this supplies the household scene behind Pharaoh’s later claim in 26:18.

luna: This continues Moses’s infancy scene: after he refuses other nurses, his sister directs Pharaoh’s household to his mother, completing the return to nurture that the section sets against Pharaoh’s boast.
luna: This completes Moses’s return to his mother in 28:12; the ayah says God restored him to her so she could be comforted and know God’s promise was true.
luna: The section links Moses’s “lost” wording in 26:20 to his past; in this separate account he admits he wronged himself after striking a man and asks his Lord to forgive him.
luna: Continuing Moses’s admission in 28:15, this ayah says God forgave him, a specific instance of the Lord’s gift after his error.
terra: Moses leaves the city fearful and asks his Lord to save him from the wrongdoing people. It supplies the flight that immediately precedes his request for a level way.

luna: The section’s Moses asks for guidance on the road to Midian; this ayah has him hope that his Lord will guide him to the right way (سواء السبيل). | terra: Leaving toward Midian, Moses asks his Lord to guide him to the level way (سَوَاءَ ٱلسَّبِيلِ). It gives the section’s water-and-road scene its initial request for direction.

luna: Continuing Moses’s journey in 28:22, he reaches the well of Midian, where he finds shepherds watering and two women holding back their flock, meeting the section’s road, herd, and water. | terra: At Midian’s water Moses finds a group watering and two women holding back their flock. It supplies the missing well and herd scene between road and shade.

luna: After watering the flock in 28:23, Moses withdraws to shade and tells his Lord that he is in need of whatever good is sent down to him; this is the section’s road, water, shelter, and dependence in one scene. | terra: After watering for them, Moses withdraws to shade and confesses need for whatever good his Lord sends. Water, shade, service, and dependence meet in one prayer.
terra: One of the women comes to invite Moses to her father, giving the well episode a human destination after his road, water, and shaded plea.
terra: Moses is offered eight years of service, with completion of ten left to him. It makes service and a chosen completion-limit part of the Midian journey’s own outcome.
terra: God’s parable asks whether people would accept their slaves as equal partners in their own provision. It clarifies why creatures cannot be co-owners with the one true master.
luna: The section’s cloud image is staged here: God sends winds that stir clouds, spreads them across the sky, and sends rain from them.
luna: This continues the moving clouds in 30:48: people rejoice when rain descends, adding the recipient’s response to the section’s provided rain.
luna: This continues 30:48’s rain: the ayah tells the Prophet to look at the traces of God’s mercy in how He revives the earth after its death.
luna: This ayah recalls a mother carrying and weaning a child and commands gratitude to God and parents, connecting the section’s nurturing image to thankfulness for favor.
luna: The section names the Lord’s gifts as visible and hidden; this ayah says God has subjected what is in the heavens and earth and poured His favors over people, both apparent and concealed.
terra: Water is driven to barren land, producing crops eaten by livestock and people. It repeats the section’s pasture-provision meeting in a land made alive.
luna: The section’s rain-and-growth image is stated here as God sending winds that raise clouds and reviving the earth after its death, a sign of resurrection as well as provision.
terra: The Prophet is declared to be upon a straight path. It gives the section’s leading guide a messenger who himself stands on the route.

luna: The section presents worship as chosen service on the path; this neighboring command forbids serving Satan and calls him a clear enemy, setting a contrary master beside God. | terra: The Children of Adam are commanded not to worship Satan, their clear enemy. It gives the section’s voluntary worship a rival master from whom the road must turn.

luna: The section joins its wording “naʿbudu” (نعبد) to the road; this ayah commands worship of God and names that worship itself “a straight path” (صراط مستقيم), making the two images one relation. | terra: “Worship Me” (وَأَنِ ٱعْبُدُونِى) is itself “a straight path”; it makes the section’s meeting of willing servitude and the requested road an explicit Qur’anic identity.
terra: Satan has led many of them astray. As the continuation of the worship/straight-path command, it gives the section’s stray ending its active misleader.

luna: The section’s herds and owner-language meet this ayah’s cattle made by God’s hands and placed under human control, with people as their owners and users. | terra: God creates livestock and makes humans their owners; it supplies the ownership side of the section’s contrast between a known Rabb and the ownerless, stray animal.
terra: “We subdued them for them” (وَذَلَّلْنَٰهَا) makes some livestock mounts and some food; the section’s tamed animal and service relation is directly enacted.
terra: Livestock provide benefits and drink; the verse completes the preceding subjugation with the provision for which the dependent servant gives praise.
terra: All things’ dominion is in God’s hand, and to Him people return. Ownership here includes the homeward return imagined at the road’s end.
luna: The section’s Day of Recompense is named here when the deniers exclaim that it is the Day of Judgment, making the reckoning scene explicit.
luna: The section’s Abraham considers celestial bodies before rejecting them as Lords; this ayah also depicts him looking toward the stars in a separate scene, a specific but less direct parallel.
terra: David must judge with truth and not follow desire lest it lead him from God’s way; the warning is punishment on the Day of Account. Judgment, path, and reckoning meet.

luna: This ayah names creation in mothers’ wombs through three layers of darkness, a specific womb image connected to the section’s formative care. | terra: God forms people in their mothers’ wombs, creation after creation, then calls Himself their Rabb whose is all dominion. Womb, nurturing Lord, and ownership coincide.
luna: The section’s willing servant addresses one Lord; this command has Muhammad say he was ordered to worship God sincerely in religion, a specific speaker stance of chosen service.
luna: This continues the sincere worship statement: Muhammad says he worships God alone, echoing the section’s direct address to its sole master.
luna: This ayah sends water down and grows crops of varied colors, then shows them yellowing and becoming debris; it joins the section’s provision image to the limit of what grows.
terra: A man owned by quarrelling partners is contrasted with one wholly belonging to one man, and the verse ends in praise. It clarifies why the section’s servant needs one true owner.

luna: The section joins the balance to people standing for judgment; this ayah depicts the book set out, prophets and witnesses brought, and judgment made in truth, supplying a concrete scene of the reckoning.
luna: This continues the judgment scene in 39:69: every soul is paid in full for what it did, a specific account-day outcome related to the section’s scales.

luna: The section’s “Owner of the Day of Recompense” makes ownership central to judgment; this ayah asks whose dominion is that day and answers that it belongs to God alone. | terra: On the Day people are exposed, God asks whose is sovereignty today and answers: the One, the Overpowering. It makes the Day’s Malikship audible.
terra: Moses seeks refuge in his Lord from every arrogant person who does not believe in the Day of Account. It connects his true Rabb to the very accounting Pharaoh’s rule denies.
luna: This ayah traces human growth from a drop to maturity and old age, linking the section’s womb and child-rearing images to development over time.
terra: People are told that their God is one, so direct themselves uprightly to Him and seek forgiveness. It joins monotheistic ownership, uprightness, and return.

luna: The section says a rising sign is not the thing it points to; this ayah explicitly forbids prostration to the sun and moon and commands prostration to God who created them. | terra: Night, day, sun, and moon are signs; people are forbidden to prostrate to sun or moon and commanded to prostrate to their Creator. This directly explains the section’s sign/referent distinction.
luna: This ayah describes the earth as humble and then stirred into growth by rain; it joins the section’s subdued ground, rain, and plant images.
luna: The section says a sign is distinct from what it points to; this ayah speaks of signs on the horizons and within people until truth is clear, a specific sign-to-reality parallel.
terra: The Prophet is told that he guides to a straight path. It gives the section’s front-going guide a prophetic, not merely animal-herd, form.

luna: This restates the section’s road image as God making earth a cradle and making paths in it so people may be guided. | terra: God makes earth a cradle and lays paths through it so people may be guided. It directly joins formed ground, road, and guidance.
terra: God sends water from the sky in due measure and revives dead land. It adds measured rain and renewal to the section’s water-and-measure meeting.
terra: God creates pairs and makes ships and livestock for riding. It joins formed creatures, travel, and animal mounts in the same divine ordering.

luna: The section joins voluntary service to travel on a mount; this ayah has riders remember that God subjected these animals and give thanks for the mount carrying them. | terra: When people settle on the backs of those mounts, they remember God’s favor and glorify the one who subjected them. The road-rider answers with praise for subjection.

luna: After the riders remember God’s subjection of their mounts in 43:13, this ayah has them say they will return to their Lord, giving the section’s traveler’s road a stated destination beyond the journey.
luna: Pharaoh boasts that Egypt and its rivers belong to him; this concrete claim to possession contrasts with the section’s true Lord and the ruler who falsely claims to have raised Moses.
luna: This says Pharaoh misled his people and they obeyed him, a specific instance of a human leader diverting a people from the way under the section’s false-master theme.
terra: Jesus’ command to worship the one Lord concludes “this is a straight path”; it gives the section’s servant-and-road image another exact formulation.

luna: The section’s “days of God” frame punishment and forgiveness; this command to believers to pardon those who do not expect God’s days connects those days with forgiving and requital. | terra: Believers are told to forgive those who do not await God’s days, when He will repay each people for what they earned. It makes those days days of moral reckoning.

luna: The section joins the womb, nurture, and a completed blessing; this ayah traces a mother’s bearing and weaning to the child reaching maturity, then has the person ask to be grateful for God’s favor. | terra: Pregnancy, weaning, reaching full strength, and gratitude for God’s favor occur in one life arc. It makes the section’s womb, maturation limit, and completed blessing concrete.
luna: This ayah names God’s anger against hypocritical men and women and associators, a specific parallel to the section’s category of those under wrath.
terra: The opponents hold back the sacrificial offering from reaching its place. This is the concrete reverse of the section’s animal being taken safely to the House.

luna: The section’s sign-and-mark image distinguishes an outward sign from what it indicates; this ayah describes a mark on believers’ faces from prostration, a specific mark that points to a devotional history. | terra: The worshippers’ mark is on their faces from prostration, while they seek God’s bounty and pleasure. It makes the section’s sign, face, worship, and rıza images meet.

luna: The section contrasts the known owner with people whose status differs by reverence; this ayah says the most honored before God is the most God-conscious, a specific limit on human ownership or lineage.
luna: The section’s term “yawm al-dīn” (يوم الدين) is explicit here as the day on which recompense occurs (لَوَاقِعٌ), a direct parallel to its account day.

luna: The section joins the heavens and the balance through the root/form “qāma”; this ayah says God raised the heaven and set the balance (الميزان) in the same statement. | terra: God raises the sky and sets the balance. It gives the section’s noon-scale image its Qur’anic meeting of height and measured equilibrium.

luna: This continues the heaven-and-balance image in 55:7: the ayah forbids transgressing in the balance, making its measure an enforceable limit. | terra: The command not to transgress the balance establishes a boundary between an upright measure and its bending or excess.

luna: Completing 55:7–8, this ayah commands establishing weight with justice and not diminishing the balance, directly meeting the section’s cheating measure. | terra: “Establish weight with justice and do not make the balance deficient” makes upright weighing the ethical counterpart to the section’s standing scale.
terra: Criminals are known by their marks and seized on the Day scene. It supplies the adverse counterpart to the worshipper’s face-mark and the favorable face.

luna: The section links the scale to people standing upright; this ayah says Scripture and the balance were sent so people might uphold justice (ليقوم الناس بالقسط), connecting the balance to q-w-m, “stand/establish.” | terra: Book and balance are sent down “so that people may stand for justice” (لِيَقُومَ ٱلنَّاسُ بِٱلْقِسْطِ). It explicitly ties measure to standing upright.
terra: Blessed is the one in whose hand is all dominion. It gives the section’s kingly hand a direct Qur’anic statement of universal ownership.

luna: The section’s dictionary form “muzallal” (مذلل) joins a subdued camel to a trodden road; here earth is made “dhulūlan” (ذلولًا, subdued/easy) and people are told to walk its paths (مناكبها). | terra: The earth is made ذَلُولًا for people to walk its shoulders and seek provision. The section’s dictionary adjective “müzellel” therefore makes tractable ground, walking, and dependence on provision meet.

luna: This ayah stages the section’s exact contrast: one walks face-down and the other walks upright on a straight path (سويًا على صراط مستقيم). | terra: The comparison is between one walking fallen on his face and one walking upright on a straight road. It is the section’s fall-versus-upright-guidance image stated bodily.
terra: “We shall brand him on the snout” gives a literal punitive mark. It is a boundary for the section’s sign image: a mark can expose disgrace rather than identify the true Lord.
luna: The section’s path begins on land; this ayah says God spread the earth out for people, preparing the ground they travel over.
luna: Continuing 71:19, this ayah says people may travel through broad paths in the earth, directly joining land and way.
terra: If they had remained upright on the way, God would have given them abundant water. The conditional makes straightness and water meet with unusual exactness.
luna: The condemned speakers say they denied the Day of Recompense; this is a direct contrary stance to the section’s reckoning day, though the ayah does not stage its balance or faces.

luna: This ayah gives the bright side of the section’s judgment-day faces: some faces that day are radiant, looking toward their Lord. | terra: Radiant faces on that Day supply another visible form of favor, strengthening the section’s claim that the Day appears on faces.

luna: This ayah sets frowning faces beside the radiant faces of 75:22, a specific facial reversal on the same judgment day. | terra: Gloomy, frowning faces expect a crushing calamity. Their expression supplies the adverse boundary to the Day’s radiant faces.
luna: This ayah says God sends pouring water from clouds, directly naming the cloud-to-rain image in the section’s account of provision.
luna: The water in 78:14 produces grain and plants here, completing a specific cloud-to-food sequence.
luna: This continues the plants of 78:15 with thick gardens, extending the section’s rain-fed provision to its visible completion.
terra: God brings forth earth’s water and pasture. This concise pairing supplies the section’s linked provision for traveller and herd.
terra: The water and pasture are provision for people and their livestock, making the prior cosmic preparation explicitly shared sustenance.
terra: Water is poured down abundantly. It begins a compact provision sequence in which rainfall is the source of the ground’s gifts.
terra: The earth is split open. It gives the received water a shaped, opening ground rather than an undifferentiated field.
terra: Grain is grown from that opened earth. It supplies a staple of the nourishment that follows water and formation.
terra: Fruit and pasture appear together. The verse directly reunites human provision with the herd’s grazing ground.
terra: The produce is enjoyment for people and their livestock. It states the shared provision that the section’s route and herd imply.
luna: The section contrasts a softened face with one covered in dust; this ayah gives the positive side as faces “bright” (مُسْفِرَةٌ) on that day.

luna: This gives the section’s dusty face literally: the ayah says dust will be on faces on that day (وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ عَلَيْهَا غَبَرَةٌ). | terra: “Faces that day” bear dust (عَلَيْهَا غَبَرَةٌ). It provides the section’s opposing, dust-covered face of judgment.
luna: This completes the dusty faces in 80:40 with darkness covering them, making the judgment-day face a sign of the opposite outcome from the softened one.
luna: This completes the dusty faces of 80:40–41 by identifying them as disbelievers and wicked-doers, giving the section’s adverse face a stated moral outcome.

luna: The section’s final camel is detached from its owner; this ayah has prized pregnant camels abandoned at the upheaval, a concrete but uncertain parallel because the reason for abandonment differs.
terra: The human being is asked what deceived them about their generous Rabb. It makes the section’s true Lord a question of recognition before the Day of Recompense.
terra: The Rabb creates, forms, and balances the human being. Formation and upright proportion meet before the passage turns to reckoning.
terra: God composes the human in whatever form He wills. It contributes the deliberate shaping behind the section’s womb-and-sign imagery.
terra: The passage immediately says people deny the Day of Recompense. It binds formed humanity to the dīn-day named in the section.
luna: This ayah says the deniers will enter the Fire on the Day of Recompense, giving a specific adverse outcome for the day named in the section.
luna: This continues 82:15 by saying they will not be absent from it, making the judgment consequence lasting.

luna: The section’s “Day of Recompense” is stated explicitly here as “what is the Day of Recompense?” (وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا يَوْمُ الدِّينِ), opening the account-day scene. | terra: The question “What will make you know the Day of Recompense?” makes dīn the Day’s active reckoning, clarifying the section’s debt-day sense.
luna: This repeats and emphasizes the question in 82:17 about the Day of Recompense, giving the section’s named day a distinct boundary before its answer.

luna: This answers the repeated question in 82:17–18: no soul can avail another on that day, and command belongs to God, directly meeting the section’s ownership and reckoning. | terra: On that Day no soul controls anything for another, and command belongs wholly to God. It supplies the section’s kingly ownership at the close of debt.

luna: The section ties cheating in measure to the day people stand before the Lord; this ayah opens the same passage by condemning those who give short measure. | terra: “Woe to the defrauders” introduces the scene in which a tilted measure becomes a matter for the Lord of all worlds.

luna: This continues the short-measure scene of 83:1: the ayah specifies that the cheaters take full measure when others measure for them, sharpening the section’s reversal between taking and giving. | terra: Those who take full measure from people enact the receiving side of the section’s balance-and-debt image.

luna: The section points to fraudulent weighing before the day of standing; this ayah completes the fraud by saying they give less when they themselves measure or weigh for others. | terra: When they measure or weigh for others, they cause loss. This is the precise reversal of the level scale the section invokes.
terra: The defrauders are asked whether they think they will be raised; their practical fraud is turned toward the standing of the Day.
terra: “That tremendous Day” names the horizon that turns ordinary weighing into final accountability.

luna: This is the section’s stated endpoint for 83:1–3: it names the day people stand before the Lord of the worlds, joining the cheated scale to the reckoning day. | terra: People will stand (يَقُومُ) before the Lord of the worlds. It directly joins the section’s qiyām image, balance, and the Rabb of 1:2.
luna: This ayah identifies those who deny the Day of Recompense, a specific opposing stance to the section’s account day.
terra: The radiance of bliss is recognizable in their faces. This turns the section’s “mark” and favorable Day-face into a visible sign of final provision.
terra: “Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High” joins the section’s opening name to elevation and praise before the Rabb.
terra: The one who creates and proportioned supplies the section’s image of a Rabb who fits a creature for its course.
terra: The one who determines and then guides puts measure and way together, reinforcing the section’s scale and guidance meeting.
terra: The one who brings out pasture supplies the plant and herd provision that follows formation and guidance.
terra: The green pasture becomes dark stubble. It provides a boundary within the section’s nourishing landscape: what is raised also passes.
luna: The section’s paired judgment faces include one softened and one under dust; this ayah describes faces humbled on that day, the adverse posture that contrasts with 88:8’s ease.
luna: This continues the humbled faces in 88:2: they are laboring and exhausted, making the adverse face an embodied condition alongside the section’s ease-filled face.

luna: The section calls one judgment-day face “nāʿimah” (ناعمة, soft/at ease); this ayah uses the same word for faces enjoying ease that day. | terra: “Faces that day will be naʿimah” (نَاعِمَةٌ), soft or blissful. It is the section’s named face on the favorable side of the Day.
luna: This continues the eased faces of 88:8: they are satisfied with their striving, giving the section’s favorable face a stated cause and response.

luna: The section pairs judgment with approval and anger; this ayah addresses the tranquil soul, a specific inner state that prepares the return to its Lord in the following verses. | terra: The tranquil soul appears at the end of judgment. It gives the favorable side of the Day an inward condition before its return.

luna: This completes 89:27’s address by inviting the soul to return to its Lord pleased and pleasing, a concrete meeting of the section’s Lord and favor. | terra: The soul is told to return to its Lord, pleased and pleasing. Divine pleasure, response, and return to the Rabb converge explicitly.
terra: The returned soul is told to enter among God’s servants. Its own contribution is the fulfilled belonging of the willing servant.
terra: The final command is to enter God’s Paradise. It supplies a home beyond the road for the returning, pleased soul.
terra: God found the Prophet an orphan and gave shelter; this supplies a non-Pharaonic image of the Rabb’s unclaimed, protective nurture.

luna: The section’s lost-way image meets the wording “He found you lost and guided you” (ضَالًّا فَهَدَى); the verse does not stage a lost traveler, so this is a specific lexical parallel whose precise sense is uncertain. | terra: “Found you ضَالًّا and guided” places lostness and guidance inside that same merciful care, like the section’s stray animal found by its true guide.
terra: “Found you in need and made you self-sufficient” completes the trio with provision, clarifying what true divine upbringing gives without reproach.
terra: “Read in the name of your Lord who created” makes a named Rabb the source of creation, matching the section’s beginning with a name and its formative Lord.
terra: The final garden reward culminates in God being pleased with them and they with Him. It gives rıza its mutual, eschatological completion.

luna: This ayah makes the section’s weighing image an outcome at judgment: whoever’s scales are heavy has a pleasing life. | terra: One whose scales are heavy receives a pleasing life; this makes weight on the Day a lived result rather than an abstraction.

luna: This is the other side of 101:6: light scales lead to an abyss, giving the section’s balance a specific boundary between outcomes. | terra: One whose scales are light has the abyss as mother. It adds the catastrophic reverse of the section’s balanced standing.
